decision.reason: The requested internal surfaces are hookable, especially on Granite, but no cached internal activations exist to test whether any surface has strict set-leaving below 0.30. Existing block-output references remain high drift at 0.566 for Granite-Small and 0.674 for Falcon-H1.

tiny_gpu_sanity_request.priority: Granite first; Falcon only if Granite identifies a low-drift internal surface.
tiny_gpu_sanity_request.traces: 2 deterministic release drift traces are enough for hook sanity; use 12 only if already cheap.
implementation_notes: Use PyTorch/HF eager diagnostic path, not vLLM serving kernels.
Force the unfused Mamba Python path for hookability by disabling the module-level fast-path flag before execution.
Persist per-channel absolute magnitude summaries at requested positions, not full token-by-layer activations.
Compute strict top-1% set-leaving relative to position 100 for each trace, layer, and surface.

promotion_rule.promote_msurface_if: At least one internal Granite surface has strict set-leaving < 0.30 while the same run's post-block output stays near the cached high-drift regime.
promotion_rule.kill_or_defer_if: All hookable internal surfaces are >= 0.30, within roughly 0.10 absolute of block-output drift, or only B/C appears lower with unstable top-k due to the 256-dimensional surface.
promotion_rule.falcon_followup_if: Only repeat on Falcon-H1 after Granite shows a materially lower internal surface.
